newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel urges MOF to form tight 1997/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel urges MOF to form tight 1997/98 budget.

text.p: An advisory panel under the Ministry of Finance (MOF) urged the ministry on Thursday to form a tight budget which will reduce the nation's dependency on public bonds to finance the state budget.

"We urge the government to step up efforts to carry out reforms and drastically reduce spending," according to the proposals made by Financial System Council for the state budget for the fiscal year starting on April 1.

"At the same time, we need to pave the way for lowering our dependency on public bonds (to finance the state budget) by reducing public bond issues as much as possible and ending our reliance on deficit-financing bonds early in the 21st century," the statement said.
It said it was "extremely regrettable" that the government had to depend on deficit-financing bonds to fund the state budget this fiscal year and most likely would have to again next year.
Japan should make efforts to reduce bond issues, especially of deficit-financing bonds, not only this year, but in following years to lower the dependency on public bonds.
It also urged Japan to suppress general spending, the core of the state budget, as much as possible.

Concerning a possible supplementary budget for this fiscal year, the statement said the government should review the traditional method of resorting to public works spendings to boost its economy and avoid additional issues of deficit-financing bonds.
